note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: France: revenue-section vote postponed to Oct 27 (formal vote Nov 3); 2,000+ amendments pending; OAT-Bund ~146bp; Moody's reviews France Friday. US shutdown day 20 (11th failed Senate vote).
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US session: housing starts 1.221M missed (vs 1.30M), pending home sales -7.3% (record-low index 66.0), ADP weekly cooled to 18.5K — the housing soft patch vs last week's retail (+0.8%) and IP (+0.7%) beats. Asia: AI doubts hit hard (Kospi -3.7%, Nikkei -1.3%).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: German Sep PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%) Tuesday. US demand cratered even as inflation runs hot (CPI 3.7%, imports +8.1% y/y). UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%); NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC Oct 27-28: hold ~84-85% (CME FedWatch Oct 20); December hike 88-90% — up from the stale 70.3%. BoC Oct-28 hike ~85-87% (LSEG ~85%, CORRA OIS 87%; the Oct-19 '78% hold-bet' is superseded). RBNZ Oct-28 hike 80-89% (to 3.00%). ECB Oct 29: hold ~97-98%; Dec hike 84%. BoE Nov 5: hike 95%. BoJ Oct 29-30: hold ~94%+; Dec hike ~73%.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 13 report): all G10 signals neutral (0). Splits: hedge funds flipped AGAINST the yen while real money bets FOR it; hedge funds for the Aussie but real money strongly against. Funds strongly short CAD (added sharply). No crowded-long unwind risk anywhere — the pain trade is two-sided.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Mixed Tuesday: AI skepticism (Kospi -3.7%) bid the dollar early (DXY 101.69, -0.27%), but the NY session faded it — EUR +0.2%, GBP +0.66% on the jobs beat. No haven bid from geopolitics (no retaliation, no confirmed Saudi damage).
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent Dec ~$110.07 (+0.5%) after a five-month high of $111.75 on the Houthi Saudi claims (unconfirmed by Riyadh); WTI Nov expired in a squeeze (~$109) — the Dec contract ~$98.9 is the clean read; Brent-WTI ~$11. Gold ~$4,120-4,135 (3rd down day).
tot.title: Terms of trade
